result.title: ForeSay: Tell the Future in Words, Branch the Details in Noise for Precipitation Nowcasting
result.summary: Precipitation nowcasting involves two distinct scales of uncertainty: macroscopic storm evolution and fine-scale local convective variations. Current generative ensemble methods entangle both scales within independent random noise draws. This coupling causes two practical limitations: every ensemble member must execute the full sampling trajectory from scratch, so an N-member ensemble costs N times a single forecast; moreover, divergent trajectories spatially misalign heavy-rain echoes across members, causing standard pixel-wise averaging to blur critical high-intensity extremes. We present ForeSay, a generative nowcasting framework that decouples macroscopic evolution prediction from local stochastic detail generation. Given historical radar frames, a vision-language model first predicts a textual scenario of future storm dynamics to condition a Rectified Flow generator. Guided by this shared macroscopic prior, ensemble members share early trunk sampling steps to establish the storm trajectory and branch with fresh noise only in later steps to explore local convective details. Because members then differ mainly in local details, self-anchored support-consensus decoding replaces pixel averaging with discrete support voting to preserve sharp heavy-rain cores. Across six datasets, ForeSay achieves the best CSI at the highest precipitation thresholds, with relative improvements over the strongest baseline on each dataset ranging from over 10% to 84%. Our 8-member ensemble retains the forecasting skill and diversity of eight independently sampled runs while reducing computational cost from 8x to 5.2x that of a single forecast.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 ForeSay 降水临近预报框架，用视觉语言模型先预测未来风暴演变的文本情景作为宏观先验去条件化 Rectified Flow，并让集成成员共享早期采样步、仅在后期分支出新噪声，再以支持度投票解码代替像素平均。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「宏观情景先验 + 局部随机细节」的解耦与共享前缀采样后分支的做法，可能为 LVR 中区分任务必要状态与随机细节、以及共享 latent 轨迹下的多分支探索与成本—多样性权衡提供可核查线索，但不直接研究多模态推理。
